titleStmt.title: Letter from Curtis Brown LtdLimited Liability to Leonard Woolf, March 16, 1933.: A machine-readable transcription
titleStmt.principal: Prof. dr. Adriaan van der Weel

bibl.title: Letter from Curtis Brown LtdLimited Liability to Leonard Woolf, 16 March, 1933.

projectDesc.p: Prepared by students of the 2025-2026 The Book in the Digital Age: Agents and Medium course, Book and Digital Media Studies, Leiden University

div.p: In this letter addressed to Leonard Woolf, husband to Virginia Woolf, Curtis Brown Ltd inquires about the possibilities of publishing Mrs. Woolf's new work in "Time and Tide". Further organisations are mentioned as not being viable options for the format of her writing. A projection of the timeline is outlined and a cost for the First British Serial Rights is provided.

I have been working daily on the serial situa-
tion with reference to "FLUSH
Novel by Virginia Woolf." As you know, "Good
Housekeeping
American Magazine" have now reluctantly come to the final
conclusion - as was the case previously with "Woman's
Journal
American women's rights periodical published from 1870-1931" - that the subtle qualities of this work
could not be sufficiently well conveyed in monthly
instalments to make a monthly magazine a suitable
medium. This view I find is shared by the editor of
the "Strand
British monthly magazine published 1891 to 1950", in spite of the fact that he is anxiously
seeking for material of a somewhat less obvious nature
than that which they have tended to run in the past:
and was therefore particularly grateful for being given
the opportunity of considering the present MSManuscript.

There are still such mediums as the "Telegraph
British daily broadsheet newspaper"
and "Evening Standard
Daily tabloid newspaper in London" with whom one might discuss the
possibilities - though their space is, generally speak-
ing, very restricted at present:- but first I shall be
glad to know how you view the following suggestion which
comes from "Time and Tide
Periodical":-

I am frequently asked by Lady Rhondda
Refers to Margaret Haig Thomas, the 2nd Viscountess Rhondda, who was an essayist, autobiographer, and suffragette to give her
the chance of acquiring material of first-class impor-
tance: on the understanding that she will endeavour, in
such cases, to put forward offers at a considerably higher
rate than that ruling in the weekly field as a whole: and
I therefore rang her up tentatively in the matter the
other day: without, that is to say, actually showing her
the MS.Manuscript until I knew how you would view "Time and Tide"
as a medium. She is, as I anticipated, intensly
interested, and is asking whether - Mrs.Missus Woolf
having agreed that it might be out for serial pur-
poses - she would consider a proposal to run, say,
roughly Twenty Thousand Words in seven parts at
Seventy-Five Pounds for First British Serial Rights
only:- with the further possibility of running an
eighth instalment.

I think there would be no doubt but that we could
arrange publication so as to make way for the appear-
ance of the book in June, as you plan, and to arrange
further that "Time and Tide" run a line making it quite
clear that it will be published by the Hogarth Press
British publishing house founded in 1917 by Leonard Woolf and Virginia Woolf.

May I thanthen know how you would like me to proceed
with "Time and Tide" - with whom, by the way, I have
not argued at all as yet on the price basis: waiting
first to hear your views.

Miss Head, by the way, was most anxious that I
should say how keenly she is looking forward to the
chance of securing for "Good Housekeeping" the continua-
tion of "A ROOM OF ONE'S OWN
1929 essay by Virginia Woolf", if and when this materialises,
as discussed with Mrs.Missus Woolf.
